exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.form_cue: Your lifelong maintenance habit. A couple of sets before heavy or overhead days keeps everything tracking.
exercises.why: You've reclaimed your neck — these few reps are the cheap insurance that keeps the C6 nerve happy for good.

exercises.name: Multi-Direction Isometrics
exercises.form_cue: One firm round in all four directions, 8 sec holds. Quick and effective.
exercises.why: Maintains the cervical strength you've built so it never becomes the weak link again.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.form_cue: Pull apart and squeeze. A great between-sets filler on pressing days.
exercises.why: Postural maintenance for a desk worker who lifts — keeps the upper back strong and the shoulders healthy.

exercises.name: Heavy-Slow Wrist Extension
exercises.form_cue: One maintenance set or two, controlled tempo. Keep the load you finished Phase 3 with.
exercises.why: A weekly dose keeps the tendon robust. Tendons stay healthy when you keep loading them — don't drop this entirely.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.form_cue: Neutral grip, full control. Part of your normal arm training now.
exercises.why: Folds your elbow rehab into ordinary training — the rehab is done, this is just smart maintenance.

exercises.name: Squat (auto-regulated)
exercises.form_cue: Front or back squat, neutral neck, braced trunk. Pick a weight that leaves 2 reps in reserve. Add load when 4×5 feels strong.
exercises.why: Your main lower-body strength driver. Auto-regulating by reps-in-reserve keeps you progressing without grinding reps that could compromise form and your neck.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.form_cue: Neutral spine head-to-hips, brace, drive through the floor. Straps as needed. Keep 1-2 reps in reserve.
exercises.why: Total-body strength and a powerful posterior chain — the backbone of a resilient, pain-free back.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (seated or standing)
exercises.form_cue: Brace, press overhead, move your head 'through the window' without throwing it back. Standing only if it stays symptom-free — otherwise keep it seated.
exercises.why: Full overhead strength regained. You've earned this movement back through months of progressive loading — keep monitoring and it stays yours.

exercises.name: Bench Press or Weighted Dip
exercises.form_cue: Controlled range, shoulder blades set. For dips, stay upright-ish and don't sink past comfortable depth.
exercises.why: Maintains and builds upper-body pressing strength to balance all your pulling and overhead work.

exercises.name: Pull-Up or Weighted Row
exercises.form_cue: Full hang to chin (or row to ribs). Lead with the elbows, neck long. Add weight when 4×8 is easy.
exercises.why: Heavy pulling keeps the upper back and grip strong — the foundation of good posture and a healthy neck for life.

exercises.name: Loaded Carry + Core Finisher
exercises.form_cue: Farmer or suitcase carry 45 sec, then a hard plank or hanging leg raise. Tall and braced throughout.
exercises.why: Trunk and grip strength that ties your whole body together and supports both lifting and your light running.
